text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Abdullah to hold economic talks in Beirut today.
- Two Israeli helicopters raid south Lebanon.
- Islamic resistance attacks three enemy areas in south Lebanon.
- Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah says his country supports the Lebanese people's hanging on to their legitimate rights in south Lebanon.
Prince Abdullah, on the first visit by a senior Saudi official to Lebanon in nearly two decades, stressed his country's support in seeking the withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon.

- Sources close to Prime Minister Rafik Hariri say latest government decisions enough to postpone "hunger revolt"; former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili is urging residents of Bekaa Valley to start hunger strike and civil disobedience campaign on July 4 to pressure the Beirut government into easing poverty..
- U.S. senators call on their government to lift the ban on travel to Lebanon.
- Syria, Egypt and six Gulf Arab states did not reach their main objectives in talks in Syria.
- Building activity slowed during first five months of this year.
